tier: Residential IP VPS SD-2 and SD-4

free_tier.stated: No free tier. Residential IP VPS SD-2 is 'Starting from $25.00 USD Monthly': 2 CPU, 2 GB RAM, 25 GB NVMe, 2 TB bandwidth, 1 dedicated residential IP. SD-4 is $40.00 USD monthly: 4 CPU, 4 GB, 50 GB NVMe, 4 TB, 2 dedicated residential IPs. A 10-VPS bundle with 10 residential IPs and 15 TB transfer is $195.00 USD monthly, and a 254-IP node is $795.00 USD monthly. The store shows a free setup fee.
free_tier.notes: A refund window of 48 hours from payment is stated; there is no trial without payment.

retention.stated: not applicable: a rented machine and its address, not stored bytes. What happens to the address at non-payment is unverified: the store and product pages state no term for it.

egress.terms: A monthly bandwidth allowance per plan: 2 TB on SD-2, 4 TB on SD-4, 15 TB across the 10-VPS bundle at a 1 Gbps port. No overage price is stated on the pages read.
egress.free_allowance: 2 TB per month on SD-2; 4 TB per month on SD-4

interface_detail: Remote Desktop (RDP) on Windows Server 2019, 2022, 2025 or Windows 10 Home, or remote Linux, with full administrative access. The product is a machine with an address; the vendor states 'These are not a proxy'. RDP is not in the interface vocabulary, so the token is unknown.
tooling: An RDP client, or an SSH client on the Linux image, plus a proxy or tunnel daemon the user installs on the machine. The vendor publishes no proxy endpoint and no API for the residential product.
chaining: A Worker opens an outbound connection to the VPS's fixed address and the VPS makes the upstream request, so the upstream sees the address's announcing ASN instead of AS13335. The vendor names the locations Seattle, Ashburn, Los Angeles, Charlotte and New York City.

limits.value: 2 TB per month of bandwidth on SD-2, 4 TB on SD-4, 15 TB on the 10-VPS bundle

limits_note: The registration class of the delivered address is the constraint the vocabulary cannot name. The vendor labels each location with an ISP (Seattle 'AtlasNetworks', Ashburn 'Wave Broadband and Charter', New York City 'Optimum WIFI', Charlotte 'Spectrum'), and a registry lookup of three published test addresses disagrees with the label for two of them: the Seattle test address sits in a block whose ARIN registrant is 'Private Customer' under a parent held by 'Internet Utilities NA LLC' and is announced by AS21743 (Atlas Networks Corporation), and the New York City test address is registered to RCN and announced by AS6079.
binding_note: No quota binds a low-volume exit: the smallest allowance is 2 TB per month. What decides this record is the registration class of the delivered address, which the limit vocabulary has no kind for.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: the sign-up page states 'To create an account, please place an order with us', so an account exists only after checkout and the checkout fields are behind the cart. The kind records an email as the floor. The FAQ names credit-card payment, which can be held for up to 30 minutes for fraud review.

reliability_note: The vendor does not guarantee a never-used address ('usually clean and fresh but we cannot guarantee they have never been used before') and allows one address change in the first 48 hours. A forum review list reports the Atlas and Sprint ranges, some addresses hitting human-verification prompts, and free address changes with refunds.
confidence_note: Prices, allowances, locations and the refund window are documented from the vendor's store and product pages. The registry facts for three published test addresses are measured with ARIN RDAP and RIPEstat on one address per location, not on a delivered address, so the registration class of a purchased address is unverified. Identity beyond the account-at-checkout rule is unverified.

notes: Registry lookups of the published test addresses, one address per location, ARIN RDAP and RIPEstat on 2026-11-03: Seattle 209.200.234.1 is registered to a 'Private Customer' under a parent held by Internet Utilities NA LLC and announced by AS21743 Atlas Networks Corporation; New York City 67.101.108.2 is an RCN assignment announced by AS6079; Charlotte 70.63.196.2 is registered to ATS INC (announcing ASN not looked up). The Ashburn and Los Angeles addresses were not looked up. The vendor's ISP label disagrees with the registrant for the New York City address (label Optimum WIFI, RCN assignment), the Seattle registrant is a private customer and not an ISP, and the Charlotte registrant ATS INC was not tied to Spectrum by any lookup made. The record is a caveat, not a clean pass, because the class of the address a buyer receives is the vendor's choice within the stated ISP list.

extras.rung_note: The product sells a registration class and the registry lookups tested it on published test addresses only.
